subject: Deployment mode routing & migration tradeoffs — post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode routing & migration tradeoffs — post-demo clarifications

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and a few qualification items so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem) and propose a practical migration path from your current stack.

High-level takeaways from our call:
- BrightPath runs latency-sensitive inference on a legacy GPU cluster for some payment flows, and uses a mix of public LLM APIs for non-sensitive workloads.
- Compliance team needs VPC/isolation for any PII-related models; non-PII can live on reserved (Dedicated) capacity if that gives cost predictability.
- Current pain: unpredictable throttling on the public API during spikes + operational overhead maintaining the cluster.

What we need from you to recommend a target architecture:
1) Peak sustained RPS (or QPS) and typical daily/hourly distribution (spikes vs baseline).
2) Typical input sequence length distribution (median and 95th percentile in tokens).
3) Which routes must be fully private (VPC/on-prem) vs which can be hosted or dedicated?
4) Data retention and KV cache needs (do you want Redis-like cache vs per-request only?).
5) Any mandatory KMS/HSM requirements and allowed cloud regions.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.xlsx (pricing & capacity options) and BrightPath-SOC2-summary.pdf (SOC2 + compliance notes). Also attaching a short migration-playbook draft internally for our team.

Proposed next steps:
- You answer the bullets above (2–3 short bullets per item)
- We schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week (include your infra/security engineer) to discuss VPC peering, KMS options, and migration cutover strategies
- We'll prepare two options: (A) Dedicated + VPC for PII routes (hybrid) with blue/green cutover; (B) Full Private deployment if procurement requires on-premise hosting — with preliminary cost delta and timeline

If you prefer a quick form, I can paste these as single-line answers in a follow-up.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0123 | dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

--

Attachment: BrightPath-SOC2-summary.pdf (summary, 3 pages)
From: Sara Lim <sara@brightpath.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightpath.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode routing & migration tradeoffs — post-demo clarifications

Thanks Dylan — great summary. Answers below (kept short as requested):

1) Peak sustained RPS: around 350 RPS for our critical payment validation flow during peak business hours; baseline ~30 RPS overnight. We see 10–15 minute spikes when campaigns run.
2) Seq length: median ~64 tokens, 95th ~220 tokens (payment context + historical notes).
3) Private vs shared: anything touching PII (payment auth, customer profiles) needs to be in Private VPC or on-prem. Non-PII (recommendation, analytics) can go on Dedicated. We are leaning hybrid — Dedicated for non-sensitive routes + Private VPC for sensitive ones.
4) KV cache: we'd like per-customer KV cache for session continuity (think per-user short-term KV with TTL ~12 hours). Prefers Redis-like behavior if you offer managed cache.
5) KMS: must integrate with our AWS KMS; HSM optional but would be a plus for production. Allowed regions: us-west-2 primarily, us-east-1 for DR.

Procurement loop: procurement@brightpath.ai is included — they will request SOW, security questionnaire, and a vendor risk assessment.

Questions for you:
- Can your Dedicated pools be configured with VPC peering (customer VPC) and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with AWS KMS?
- For migration, do you have a recommended cutover pattern where we can run the legacy cluster + Redwood in parallel and do traffic steering by percentage? If so, what metrics do you recommend to validate parity?

Thanks — happy to jump on the technical deep-dive with Ben and Marissa.

Best,
Sara
Sara Lim
Head of Infrastructure, BrightPath AI
sara@brightpath.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode routing & migration tradeoffs — internal next steps

Folks — quick internal note after Sara's answers. Key design implications:
- 350 RPS peak + 95th token length ~220 => need capacity planning for sustained token throughput and memory (KV cache per-customer will increase working set).
- Hybrid approach (Dedicated for non-PII + Private VPC for PII) is our likely recommendation, but we need to size Dedicated pools for non-PII peak and confirm VPC peering feasibility for the private routes.

Suggested immediate actions:
1) Schedule technical deep-dive: 60–75 min. Agenda: VPC peering options, BYOK/KMS, cache architecture, traffic steering for canary/beta. Proposed slots: Thu 10–11am PT or Fri 1–2pm PT.
2) Prep migration playbook draft (attached) that covers three phases: discovery & parallel testing, phased traffic steering, cutover + rollback plan. We'll include measurement criteria: latency p95, token error rate, top-5 diffs in output scoring.
3) Pricing constraint: procurement will want a firm committed rate for Dedicated; pricing workbook has flexible tiers but we should highlight a 12-month reserved discount.

Technical asks for the deep-dive (Ben):
- Customer's current cluster architecture (GPU types, batch sizes, any custom kernel mods)
- Any model variants / quantization we should pre-validate

I'll own the technical doc and run the deep-dive. Marissa, can you handle the procurement intro and SOW logistics? Monica, please prep CS success criteria for the cutover.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference

Sara / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick answers. Confirming the plan and next steps so we all have the same playbook:

Agreed architecture recommendation (tentative):
- Hybrid: Private VPC for PII-sensitive routes (payment auth, profile lookups) + Dedicated Reserved pools for non-PII inference (recommend 12-month commit for cost predictability).

Immediate deliverables from Redwood:
- Technical deep-dive to discuss VPC peering & BYOK + migration cutover details (Ben to run). Proposed slots: Thu 2027-03-11 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 2027-03-12 13:00–14:00 PT. Please confirm availability.
- Draft SOW and procurement packet (Marissa will send an initial SOW and SLR template).
- Migration playbook draft (attached) and a proposed acceptance checklist: p95 latency within 15% of baseline, functional parity for top-5 intents, and stable KV cache TTL handling.

What we need from BrightPath before the deep-dive:
- Confirmation of preferred deep-dive slot
- Short answers for Ben's technical asks: GPU types in legacy cluster, batch sizes, and any custom runtime hooks
- Procurement contact to whom Marissa will send the SOW (procurement@brightpath.ai is included)

I'll also include a short one-page note on BYOK and AWS KMS integration prior to the call so their security team can review.

Happy to take this to the next step as soon as procurement confirms the SOW recipients and we lock a slot.

Best,
